mentions.name: Modelmathics
mentions.description: Interactive course that teaches how large language models work by having learners implement one from scratch in Python. Starting from an empty file, students write a tokenizer, a bigram model, attention, and a Transformer themselves, with tests verifying each step before moving on; at the end, published open weights run on the learner's own code. Lessons run in the mm terminal app with code kept in local files on the learner's machine, and Stage 1 (11 lessons) is live as a free private beta.
mentions.problem: Understanding how LLMs really work, addressed by having learners build every component of the model themselves rather than just following along.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I wanted to understand how LLMs really work, so I’m building Modelmathics (https://modelmathics.com) and doing every lesson myself as I go.

You start from an empty Python file and write the model yourself: a tokenizer, a bigram model, attention, a Transformer. At the end, published open weights run on your own code. Tests check each step before you move on.
mentions.author: lucasov
